correctness.rationale: Definition 1.2 in Fang et al. gives x_i >= 0, (1-t)x_i <= y_j and y_j+t*x_i <= 1 for all i,j. Taking M=max_i x_i forces 0<=M<=1, (1-t)M<=y_j<=1-tM; the decomposition (x,y)=(1-M)(0,v)+M(u,(1-t)1) with v in the q-cube and u in the union of nonzero cube faces proves the exact 2^q+2^p-1 vertex list. For center (alpha*1_p,1_q/2), alpha=(p-q*t(1-t))_+/(2p), the A-vertex squared distance is p*alpha^2+q/4. A B-vertex with k active lower entries has deficit q*t(1-t)-k*(1-2alpha), which is nonnegative for every k and identifies all equality contacts. For alpha=0, the uniform A-corner distribution has mean the proposed center; for alpha>0, mixing weight alpha on the all-ones B contact and weight (1-alpha) on independently Bernoulli(theta) A-corners, theta=(1/2-alpha*(1-t))/(1-alpha), also has that mean. The identity E||V-z||^2=R^2+||z-c||^2 proves strict global uniqueness. Critical equality and endpoints are covered. The packaged standalone checker gives exact rational corroboration on 126 parameter profiles / 81,618 vertex occurrences, independent halfspace vertex enumeration on 24 small profiles and five independent numerical epigraph optimizations; finite checks are not the universal proof.

value.rationale: The exact metric covering radius of a foundational continuous marked-poset polytope family yields a genuine phase boundary q*t*(1-t)=p inside a single combinatorial face-lattice regime. When q>4p, an open interval has radius sqrt(q)/2 inherited entirely from the 2^q-vertex lower-zero cube, while the other exponentially large class of 2^p-1 vertices becomes strictly internal; the full contact profile and unique center are classified in every dimension. This directly demonstrates that constant face structure does not control Euclidean outer-ball geometry and supplies a natural complete invariant for a continuously deforming combinatorial family. It is not an arbitrary parameter slice or a textbook substitution; the exact vertex decomposition and probability contact-certificate are structural and the threshold is dimension-ratio dependent.
